question.problem:
Change the order of integration in the double integral 
${\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}-1}^{1-{x}^{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/374acdaf337d1977f938fc66a19a8b933a4464f922c7e9fd45fd39a6cacf920e.png)

The diagram above shows the region of integration. This is a type I region, and its type I representation is

$$
D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}-1\le y\le 1-{x}^{3}\}.
$$

To change the order of integration, we need to split $D$ into two type II regions. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14154008/assets/cf06c4d0e0189b8b3e3c60af788c0aa082755db9b9fab17ed0562e79e11cabe9.png)

Notice that the right boundary of the lower region, written in the form $x=x(y),$  is 

$\,$ $x=\sqrt{y+1}.$

Also, the right boundary of the upper region, written in the form $x=x(y),$ is

$\,$ $x=\sqrt[3]{1-y}.$

So, we can write $D$ as a union of

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 0,\,0\le x\le \sqrt{y+1}\}
$$

and

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le \sqrt[3]{1-y}\}.
$$

Therefore, swapping the order of integration, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}-1}^{1-{x}^{3}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{y+1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt[3]{1-y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
